This program explores the interdisciplinary theories that inform how scientific knowledge is disseminated, perceived, and used by diverse audiences. Students will engage with topics such as message framing, perception, and persuasion; political ideologies, identity politics, and policymaking; disability studies and accessible design; health communication; and the ethics of public engagement with science. Students will develop a critical lens to analyze the impact of communication strategies on societal trust in science and policy decision-making. This certificate will prepare students to excel as science and health communicators, advocates, and policy advisors. FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE FACULTY SENATE COURSES GEC Bill 2025-2026-05A At the February 4, 2026 meeting of the General Education Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval. COURSE MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: ART101 | Two-Dimensional Studio, effective Fall 2026 Change credits, description (4 crs.) Students explore 2D art and design principles through drawing, design, painting, print, and photography. Emphasis on composition, color, iteration. (Studio) (A4) ART103 | Three-Dimensional Studio, effective Fall 2026 Change credits (4 crs.) Introduction to problems in three-dimensional organization. Observations from objects with discussion and application to simple mold and casting techniques. Introduction to the use of basic materials, clay, plaster, and wood. (Studio) (A4) ART205 | Motion Design: Designing for Time and Space, effective Fall 2026 Change course number (level), title, credits, description (4 crs.) This course introduces time-based design projects for digital display, focusing on concept development, compositing, and the production of animated digital forms, including video, photography, sound, and interactivity. (Studio) (A4) ART404 (DSP404) | Data Visualization and Infographics Design, effective Fall 2026 Change credits, prerequisites (4 crs.) Cross-listed as (ART), DSP 404. (Studio) Pre: junior or senior standing. Not for graduate credit. (A4)

GER202 | Intermediate German II, effective Fall 2026 Change course number, description, prerequisites (3 crs.) Solidify intermediate-language skills while exploring other and one's own culture(s) from multiple perspectives.
Topics include roller coasters, activism, Switzerland, and German-American relations. (Seminar/Online) Pre: GER102 or GER112 or equivalent.
Not open to students with credit for GER 214, or to students who have studied German for more than four years (HS) or semesters (college) within the last six years or who are native or heritage speakers of German, unless special permission is provided. Students explore engineering disciplines, professional pathways, and college resources, building a foundation for future coursework. (Lec. 1, Rec. 1) (A4) EGR106 | Matlab for Engineering Applications, effective Summer 2026 Change title and description (2 crs.) (A4) ELE480 | Capstone Design I, effective Fall 2026 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Application of engineering skills; teams focus on the design and communication of solutions to problems with real-world constraints (may include aspects of other engineering disciplines).
First of a two-course sequence. (Lec. 2, Lab. 3) Pre: Minimum GPA average of 2.0 (C) in ELE212, ELE313, and ELE338.
Credit in ELE339 and either ELE205 or ELE208, and permission of instructor.

Not for graduate credit. (D1) COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES: BIO102 | Principles of Biology II, effective Fall 2026 Change description (3 crs.) The principles of ecology and evolution, with an emphasis on the diversity of life.

An introduction to the economics of waterborne movement of cargo (shipping and port operations, markets and innovations in maritime transportation systems, and the interplay of the operators, shipping, and ports) (Lec. 3) Pre: MAF100 or EEC105 or permission of the instructor. (B4) (C2) SUS102 (EVS102, GEO102, NRS102) | Introduction to Sustainability, effective Fall 2026 Temporary course to permanent, add cross-listings, qualify for A1 (3 crs.) Introduces sustainability science through the integrated study of Earth, ecological, and human systems, exploring global challenges such as climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity loss, and resource management through systems thinking and real-world solutions. Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee CBUM Informational/Editorial Report #2025-2026-02 February 19, 2026 Faculty Senate Meeting Approved by CBUM 1/15/26 Approved by FSEC 1/23/26 Editorial change: Bachelor of Interdisciplinary Studies (BIS) has moved from Feinstein College of Education to the College of Arts and Sciences and the following University Manual sections that reference the BIS are to be removed: 3 .40.16, 4.80.10, 5.80.10, 5.80.12-13, 5.81.10-11 and section 8.15.11 is to be revised in reference to the BIS.
Changes shall take effect immediately upon acceptance by the Faculty Senate.
Bill reference for BIS: Bill #24-25-02 Bill reference for Alan Shawn Feinstein College of education: Bill #22-23-40D Remove: 3.40.16 The Dean of the Alan Shawn Feinstein College of Education and Professional Studies shall appoint General Faculty members as instructors for special BIS courses with the approval of the appropriate department chairperson and college dean.
The Dean shall appoint temporary lecturers for special BIS courses upon recommendation of the BIS Special Faculty Committee.

The Dean may reappoint temporary lecturers for the BIS Pro-Seminar. #15-16-15D , #16-17-21, #20-21-36 Remove: 4.80.10 The Bachelor of Interdisciplinary Studies Faculty .
The membership shall consist of full-time faculty members of those departments whose courses support one or more of the BIS concentrations . #24-25-20 Remove: 5.80.10 The Bachelor of Interdisciplinary Studies (BIS) Curriculum Committee shall review all proposals for (1) the creation, modification, or abolition of BIS concentrations; (2) the modification of the general education component of the BIS program; and (3) the creation, modification or abolition of BIS courses.
The Dean of the Alan Shawn Feinstein College of Education and Professional Studies also shall review all such proposals.

In the spirit of section 8.81.20 , the BIS Curriculum Committee shall review plans for each offering of the open-ended BIS Seminars. #10-11–14 Remove: 5.80.12 The membership shall comprise two members of the Interdisciplinary Studies Faculty representing each BIS concentration, elected by the faculty of the departments which support the concentration, and one elected representative of the temporary lecturers who are teaching sections of the BIS Pro-Seminar at the time of the election.
The Dean of the Alan Shawn Feinstein College of Education and Professional Studies (or designee) shall serve as an advisor to the committee.
The committee shall elect its own chairperson.
Members of the committee shall be elected for two-year terms and may succeed themselves once. #10-11–14
